news.title: World Cup winner admits to 'impressive' Anfield dream
news.lede: Liverpool's reputation as one of the biggest clubs in the world remains intact, despite their struggles on the pitch last season. After winning the Premier League title in his first season in charge, Arne Slot led the Reds to an extremely disappointing fifth place finish last campaign. The Dutchman was relieved of his duties as a result and has now been replaced by Andoni Iraola. Iraola has enjoyed a steady start to life at Liverpool, but the Reds are still a long way from the top, but that hasn't stopped the club from receiving plenty of praise from around the footballing world.

news.title: Former World Cup star, 43, now working as cattle rancher after horror car crash and retirement from football
news.lede: ICONIC World Cup and Champions League star Oscar Cardozo has swapped football’s bright lights for a simple life as a cattle rancher in Paraguay. Cardozo, 43, rolled credits on a glittering 23-year career, which saw him standing out for Benfica and Paraguay, only last April as he spent the previous eight seasons playing for Libertad despite his advanced age. According to El Nacional, the legendary striker has now stepped away from football for a completely different life that sees him tending to livestock. The same report suggests the Paraguayan star has found peace in his new endeavour and is fully focused on his cows, mules and bulls.

news.title: Carlo Ancelotti Subjected to Foul-Mouthed Rant From Brazil World Cup Winner
news.lede: Former Brazil national team star Romário took aim at Carlo Ancelotti after the Seleção’s defeat to Japan on Saturday, calling for CBF president Samir Xaud to kick the Italian boss “the f--- out!” Brazil opened the November international break with a controversial 3–2 loss in Singapore that ended with red cards for both Ancelotti and Raphinha. Eyebrow-raising refereeing decisions aside, the Seleção hardly looked worthy of three points; beyond two sublime moments from Vinícius Júnior , the team inspired very little at both ends of the pitch.The five-time World Cup winner has now won just two of the last five matches, and one of those victories came against India.

news.title: Amputee Football World Cup: Ghana seek winning response against Colombia after opening-day setback
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge will be determined to bounce back from their opening-day disappointment when they take on Colombia in their second Group D encounter at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The Ghanaian side will be eager to put their campaign back on track following a 2-0 defeat to former world champions Angola in their opening fixture on Saturday. Head coach Stephen Richard Obeng and his charges now face a crucial test against Colombia at Santa Lucia 1 in Mexico, knowing that a positive result is essential to keeping their hopes of advancing to the next stage alive. Having suffered an early setback, the Black Challenge will be keen to rediscover their rhythm, sharpen their attacking threat and demonstrate greater resilience as they seek to get their campaign up and running.
